function.mechanism: Hydrates and forms a gel/viscous hydrocolloid network that structures water-rich foods and stabilizes texture.

adi.basis: EFSA 2016 concluded no need for a numerical ADI (equivalent to ADI not specified) and no safety concern at reported uses/use levels.

efsa.key_finding: Re-evaluation found agar (E406) not of safety concern at reported uses/use levels, including infant/toddler exposure scenarios assessed.

adi.basis: JECFA database lists ADI as NOT LIMITED for AGAR (INS 406).

concerns.summary: A published case report described agar-agar bezoar with gastric pouch dilation after Roux-en-Y bypass, indicating possible mechanical GI risk in susceptible anatomy/high-gelling intake contexts.

Recent review literature on seaweed polysaccharides notes remaining uncertainty around digestion/fermentation behavior and long-term effects, though agar itself is generally described as low-dispute/nontoxic.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2016 re-evaluation: no safety concern at reported uses/use levels; no numerical ADI needed.
JECFA AGAR entry: ADI NOT LIMITED.
Randomized pediatric trial including gelose (agar-agar) reported treatment as safe, with adverse events not attributed to study medication.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA reported highest modeled exposures in infants/toddlers, but no numerical ADI was set and no safety concern was concluded at reported use levels.

risk_assessment.rationale: Major regulatory bodies converge on low toxicological concern (EFSA no numerical ADI needed; JECFA ADI not limited; US Part 184 GRAS framework). Residual risk signals are contextual and mechanical rather than evidence of systemic toxicity at typical food-use exposures.
key_factors: EFSA 2016 no-safety-concern conclusion with no numerical ADI
JECFA ADI NOT LIMITED for AGAR (INS 406)
FDA GRAS-affirmed listing under 21 CFR 184.1115 with specified use limits
No IARC classification found for agar in current classified-agent dataset
Only isolated contextual adverse-case report (bezoar) rather than broad toxic signal
